questions.question: The two axes in flexbox are:
questions.explanation: flex-direction sets the main axis; the cross axis is perpendicular. justify-content acts on main, align-items on cross.

questions.question: flex-direction: column makes the main axis:
questions.explanation: row/row-reverse are horizontal; column/column-reverse are vertical main axes.

questions.question: justify-content: space-between distributes items with:

options.text: Equal space BETWEEN items, first at start, last at end
Equal space AROUND each item (including edges)

questions.explanation: space-between pushes first/last to edges, equal gaps between. space-around adds half-gaps at edges; space-evenly equalizes all gaps.

questions.question: align-items: stretch (default) makes items:

options.text: Fill the cross-axis (e.g. equal-height columns) when no explicit cross size is set

questions.explanation: Default align-items:stretch stretches items across the cross axis — that's why flex columns are equal height by default.

questions.question: A flex container's direct children become:

options.text: Flex items (blockified, participating in flex layout)

questions.explanation: Children of display:flex are flex items; their display value is blockified (inline elements behave as blocks).

questions.question: flex-basis: auto means the item's base size is:

options.text: Its width/height (or content size if not set)

questions.explanation: flex-basis:auto uses the element's main-size (width for row) if set, else content size — the usual default before grow/shrink.

questions.question: flex-grow distributes:

options.text: Remaining FREE space among items proportional to their grow factors

questions.explanation: After bases are laid out, positive free space is shared per flex-grow. A grow of 2 gets twice a grow of 1.

questions.explanation: Both axes need centering: justify-content (main) + align-items (cross). This is the canonical flex-centering recipe.
